card.name: Linking words before drug class names
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as receiving, to, with, or Agents that come right before a named drug or drug class. Typical settings are interaction headings and patient-exposure sentences in drug labels.

modes.label: NSAID heading
modes.description: The word Agents ending the heading Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Agents in drug interaction sections.
modes.example: 7.3 Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory<< Agents>> Including Selective Cyclooxygenase-

modes.label: Patients receiving a drug
modes.description: A verb or preposition such as receiving, to, or exposed to, placed just before a named drug or class.
modes.example: in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus<< receiving>> SGLT2 inhibitors, including can

modes.label: Inside a drug name
modes.description: The middle of a drug name, such as the lo in diclofenac.
modes.example: Avoid the use of dic<<lo>>fenac sodium and misoprostol

card.writes: No clear link to the promoted tokens. The suppressed tokens are all immune-related word starts, so it mainly steers the next word away from immun-/imm- terms.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words just before a drug or drug class is named.
